No — there's nothing to bypass. The `15_climate` module (both `magicc7_ar6` and `off` realizations) never has an `equations.gms` phase in the first place, so nothing is being circumvented.

- `modules/15_climate/module.gms` only includes `declarations`, `datainput`, and `postsolve` phases for `magicc7_ar6` (`off` doesn't even have `postsolve`).
- Everything the module produces (`p15_forc_magicc`, `pm_globalMeanTemperature`, `pm_globalMeanTemperatureZeroed1900`, `pm_temperatureImpulseResponseCO2`) is declared as a `parameter`, not a GAMS optimization `variable`. MAGICC runs as an external R/Fortran process between iterations, and its output is pulled in via `Execute_Loadpoint` in `postsolve.gms` — there's no equation block for these because they're never part of the LP/NLP.
- `pm_taxCO2eq` is likewise a core parameter (`core/declarations.gms`), directly overwritten in `postsolve.gms` when `cm_iterative_target_adj eq 2` (magicc-specific rescaling toward `s15_gr_forc_os`/`s15_gr_forc_nte`). The comment at `modules/15_climate/magicc7_ar6/postsolve.gms:87` even notes other adjustment modes (5/7/9) happen instead in `modules/45_carbonprice/functionalForm/postsolve.gms` — same pattern: a parameter overwritten post-solve, no equation involved.

So the mechanism you're describing (parameters set directly in postsolve based on `cm_iterative_target_adj`) is real and always active for whichever value that switch takes — but it's not "bypassing" `equations.gms`, since climate outputs were never equation-constrained variables to begin with.
